p.src: Meanwhile, Lady Wang summoned the girl's mother, presented her in person with several hairpins and bracelets, and instructed her to invite a number of monks to chant sutras for the repose of her daughter's soul. Her mother kowtowed in gratitude and withdrew. As it happened, Baoyu had heard the news on returning from his meeting with Yucun. He realized at once that Jinchuan had taken her own life out of shame and resentment, and his heart was already torn with anguish. When he went inside, Lady Wang rebuked and lectured him, but he had nothing he could say in reply. Only when Baochai came in did he find an opportunity to leave. With no notion where to go, he clasped his hands behind his back and walked slowly along, head bowed, sighing as he went, until his wandering steps brought him to the main hall. He had just turned past the screen gate when someone coming in from the opposite direction unexpectedly collided squarely with him. He heard the man bark, “Stop right there!” Baoyu started in fright. Looking up, he saw that it was none other than his father. He involuntarily drew a sharp breath and could only stand to one side with his hands respectfully lowered. Jia Zheng said, “Everything is perfectly well, so why are you hanging your head and sighing so dejectedly? Yucun came just now and asked to see you. We called for you for ages before you appeared, and when you finally did, you showed not the least ease or spirit in your conversation, but remained as timid and shrinking as ever. Your face is full of brooding desire and melancholy, and now you are sighing and groaning again. Do you still not have enough? Is there still something making you unhappy? Why are you behaving like this for no reason?” Eloquent though Baoyu ordinarily was, his whole heart was now consumed with grief for Jinchuan, and he wished that very moment to die and follow her. Thus, although his father stood before him saying all this, he had not really heard a word and merely stood there in a daze.

p.src: Seeing Baoyu so frightened and finding his replies unlike their usual manner, Jia Zheng, who had not been angry to begin with, now became somewhat incensed. He was just about to speak when a steward suddenly came to report, “Someone from Prince Zhongshun's residence is here and wishes to see you, sir.” Jia Zheng was puzzled when he heard this and thought to himself, “We ordinarily have no dealings with the Zhongshun residence. Why have they sent someone today?” Even as he wondered, he ordered, “Show him in at once.” Hurrying out to see, he found that the visitor was the chief secretary of the Zhongshun residence. He promptly ushered him into the hall, seated him, and had tea served. Before they could exchange courtesies, the chief secretary began, “I have not presumed to intrude upon your distinguished residence of my own accord. I come entirely at His Highness's command to ask a favor of you. For His Highness's sake, may I trouble you, venerable sir, to settle the matter? Not only will His Highness appreciate it, but we, his servants, shall also be endlessly grateful.” Unable to make head or tail of this, Jia Zheng hurriedly rose with an accommodating smile and asked, “Since you come at His Highness's command, may I ask what instructions you bear? Please state them plainly, so that I may comply and see the matter carried out.” The chief secretary gave a cold laugh. “There is no need for you to carry anything out. A single word from you will settle it. At our residence there is a young female-role actor called Qiguan. He had always remained there without incident, but for the past several days he has failed to return. We have searched everywhere, yet cannot trace where he has gone, and so have been making inquiries in every quarter. Eight people out of ten in this city say that lately he has been on especially intimate terms with your honorable son, the young gentleman born with jade in his mouth. When we heard this, we knew that your distinguished residence was not like an ordinary household into which we might barge and demand someone, so we reported the matter to His Highness. His Highness said as well, ‘Were it any other actor, I should not care if a hundred of them vanished. But this Qiguan is quick and apt in his answers, prudent, honest, and thoroughly to my old liking. I absolutely cannot do without him.’ We therefore beg you, venerable sir, to convey the message to your son and ask him to release Qiguan. In the first place, this will answer His Highness's earnest entreaty, and in the second, it will spare us servants the labor of searching for him.” With that, he hurriedly made a deep bow.

p.src: Jia Zheng was both shocked and furious at these words and at once ordered Baoyu to be summoned. Baoyu had no idea what had happened. When he came hurrying in, Jia Zheng demanded, “You wretched slave! It is bad enough that you will not study at home. How dare you commit such outrageous, lawless deeds as these! Qiguan is presently an attendant in Prince Zhongshun's service. What kind of worthless creature are you, that you should entice him away for no reason and now bring disaster upon me?” Baoyu started in alarm and hastily replied, “I truly know nothing of this matter. I do not even know what the name ‘Qiguan’ refers to, much less how the word ‘entice’ could be applied to me!” As he spoke, he began to cry. Before Jia Zheng could speak, the chief secretary gave a cold laugh and said, “There is no need for you to conceal the truth, young sir. Whether you are hiding him here or merely know where he is, tell us at once and spare us further hardship. Would we not then be grateful for your kindness?” Baoyu repeatedly insisted that he did not know. “It may only be a false rumor; there is no telling whether it is true.” The chief secretary sneered. “We have solid evidence. Why persist in denying it? Must I disclose it here before your venerable father and cause you embarrassment? If you claim not to know the man, how did his red sash come to be around your waist?” At these words, Baoyu felt as though his soul had been blasted from his body. He stared speechlessly and thought, “How could he know of that? Since he even knows a secret like this, I probably cannot hide anything else from him. I had better send him on his way before he reveals some other matter.” He therefore said, “Since you know so much about him, how can you be unaware of so important a matter as his purchase of a house and land? I have heard that at a place called Zitan Fort in the eastern suburbs, some twenty li from the city, he has bought several mu of land and a few houses. He may perhaps be there.” The chief secretary smiled when he heard this. “If that is so, he must certainly be there. I shall go and look for him. If I find him, that will be the end of it; if I do not, I shall have to return and seek your further guidance.” With that, he hurried away.

p.src: Jia Zheng was now so enraged that his eyes stared and his mouth twisted. While seeing the chief secretary out, he turned and ordered Baoyu, “Do not move! I shall have questions for you when I return!” He then escorted the official all the way out. No sooner had he turned back than he saw Jia Huan dashing wildly about with several pages. Jia Zheng shouted at the pages, “Beat him! Beat him at once!” At the sight of his father, Jia Huan was so frightened that his bones seemed to melt and his sinews go limp; he hurriedly lowered his head and stood still. Jia Zheng demanded, “What are you running for? None of the people assigned to you looks after you; goodness knows where they have wandered off, leaving you to run wild like an untamed horse!” He ordered that those who accompanied Jia Huan to school be summoned. Seeing his father in a towering rage, Jia Huan seized the opportunity to say, “I was not running at first. But as I passed the well just now, I saw that a maid had drowned in it. Her head had swollen this large and her body this thick—it was truly horrible. That is why I came running away.” Startled and suspicious, Jia Zheng asked, “Why would anyone jump into a well for no reason? Nothing of this kind has ever happened in our household. Since our ancestors’ time, servants have always been treated with leniency and kindness. No doubt I have grown negligent in household affairs these past few years, allowing those in charge to wield harsh and oppressive authority, until this calamity of a life so recklessly destroyed has come about. If outsiders learn of this, what will become of our ancestors’ good name?” He shouted for Jia Lian, Lai Da, and Lai Xing to be summoned at once. The pages answered and were just about to fetch them when Jia Huan hurried forward, caught hold of Jia Zheng’s robe, knelt close against his knees, and said, “Father, please do not be angry. Apart from the people in Madam’s apartments, no one knows anything about this. I heard my mother say…” At this point he turned and looked all around. Understanding his meaning, Jia Zheng glanced at the pages. They took the hint and withdrew to the sides and rear. Jia Huan then whispered, “My mother told me that the other day, in Madam’s apartments, Brother Baoyu seized Madam’s maid Jinchuan’er and tried to force himself upon her. When he failed, she was beaten. In anger and humiliation, Jinchuan’er threw herself into the well and died.” Before he had finished, Jia Zheng’s face turned as pale as gold paper with rage, and he roared, “Bring Baoyu here at once!” As he spoke, he strode toward the inner study, shouting, “If anyone tries to dissuade me again today, I shall hand over my cap and girdle, this household, and all its property to him, and let him live with Baoyu! I shall have no choice but to become a sinner, shave off these few troublesome hairs, and seek some pure place in which to end my days, thereby escaping the guilt of disgracing my ancestors above and begetting a rebellious son below.” When the retainers and servants saw Jia Zheng in this state, they knew it was once again on Baoyu’s account. Every one of them bit his finger and tongue in alarm and hastily withdrew. Jia Zheng sat bolt upright in his chair, panting heavily, his face streaked with tears, and cried again and again, “Bring Baoyu! Bring the heavy cudgel! Bring ropes and bind him!”

p.src: When Baoyu heard Jia Zheng order him not to move, he already knew that little good and much evil awaited him; he could never have expected Jia Huan to add so many accusations. He paced helplessly around the hall, wondering how he might find someone to carry a warning inside; perversely, not a soul was there, and even Beiming was nowhere to be found. Just as he was anxiously hoping for someone, an old nurse came out. Baoyu felt as though he had found a treasure. He hurried after her, caught hold of her, and said, “Quickly, go inside and tell them: Master is going to beat me! Go quickly, quickly! It is urgent—terribly urgent!” For one thing, Baoyu was so frantic that he spoke indistinctly; for another, the old woman happened to be deaf. She did not catch what he was saying at all, but mistook the words “it is urgent” for “jumped into the well.” Laughing, she said, “If she wants to jump into the well, let her. What is Second Master afraid of?” Realizing that she was deaf, Baoyu said in desperation, “Then go outside and call my page for me.” The old woman said, “What remains unsettled? It was all settled long ago. Madam gave clothes as a reward and silver besides. How could the matter not be settled?”

p.src: Baoyu stamped his feet in desperation, utterly at a loss. Just then Jia Zheng’s pages arrived and forced him to go out with them. The instant Jia Zheng saw him, his eyes turned dark red with fury. He did not even stop to question him about consorting with an actor outside, exchanging private gifts, neglecting his studies at home, or dishonouring his mother’s maid. He merely roared, “Gag him and beat him soundly to death!” The pages dared not disobey. They had no choice but to pin Baoyu down on a bench, raise the heavy paddle, and strike him more than ten times. Jia Zheng still thought they were striking too lightly. He kicked the man wielding the paddle aside, snatched it from him, clenched his teeth, and brought it down with all his might another thirty or forty times. When the retainers saw that the beating had taken an ominous turn, they hurried forward to wrest the paddle away and plead with him to stop. But Jia Zheng would not listen. “Ask him whether the deeds he has committed can be forgiven! It is all of you who have spoiled him day after day, and even now, when things have come to this pass, you still try to intercede for him. Will you not cease your pleading until you have encouraged him to murder his sovereign and kill his father?”

p.src: Finding these words ominous and realizing that Jia Zheng was beside himself with rage, they hurriedly withdrew again and had no choice but to find someone to carry word inside. Lady Wang dared not report first to Grandmother Jia. She hurriedly dressed and came out, paying no heed to who might be present, then hastened toward the study so abruptly that the retainers and pages barely managed to get out of her way. The moment Lady Wang entered the room, Jia Zheng's fury flared as though oil had been poured upon fire, and his blows fell harder and faster than ever. The two pages holding Baoyu down hastily released him and stepped aside; by then Baoyu could no longer move. When Jia Zheng tried to strike him again, Lady Wang seized the board. “Enough, enough!” cried Jia Zheng. “You are all determined to hound me to death today!” Lady Wang wept, “Though Baoyu deserves punishment, you must take care of yourself, my lord. Besides, in this scorching summer weather the old lady is not in the best of health. Baoyu's death would be a small matter, but if the old lady were suddenly taken ill, would that not be far graver?” Jia Zheng sneered, “Do not speak to me of that. By begetting this unworthy monster I have already proved unfilial; yet when I try to discipline him, everyone rallies to protect him. I may as well strangle him today and put an end to future trouble!” With that, he called for a rope with which to strangle him. Lady Wang hastily clung to him and cried, “Though you have every right to discipline your son, my lord, you must show some regard for the bond between husband and wife. I am nearly fifty now, and this wretch is the only son left to me. If you are determined to make a severe example of him, I dare not plead too strongly. But now you mean to kill him outright—is that not as good as deliberately ending my life too? If you intend to strangle him, bring the rope quickly and strangle me first, then him. Neither mother nor son will bear you any resentment; at least in the underworld we shall have each other to depend upon.” Having said this, she threw herself over Baoyu and burst into loud sobs. At these words Jia Zheng heaved a long sigh, sank into a chair, and wept torrents. Holding Baoyu in her arms, Lady Wang saw that his face was pallid and his breath faint. The green gauze undergarment covering his lower body was stained all over with blood. Unable to restrain herself, she untied his sash to look: from buttocks to shins he was blue and purple, the skin in places intact and in places split, without a single uninjured spot. She cried out in anguish, “Oh, my ill-fated child!” Her cry of “my ill-fated child” suddenly brought Jia Zhu to mind. Calling his name, she sobbed, “If only you were still alive, I should not care even if a hundred of me were to die.” By this time, those in the inner apartments had heard that Lady Wang had gone out, and Li Gongcai, Wang Xifeng, Yingchun, and the other young ladies had already followed. As Lady Wang wept and called Jia Zhu's name, the others managed to contain themselves, but Gongcai alone could bear it no longer and began sobbing aloud as well. Hearing this, Jia Zheng's tears rolled down all the faster, like melons tumbling from a cart. While the turmoil was still at its height, a maid suddenly came in to announce, “The old lady is here.”

While the turmoil was still at its height, a maid suddenly came in to announce, “The old lady is here.”

p.src: Before she had finished speaking, a trembling voice was heard outside the window: “Kill me first, and then kill him—then everything will be nice and tidy!” Seeing that his mother had come, Jia Zheng was both alarmed and distressed and hurried out to meet her. Grandmother Jia was approaching, leaning on a maid and gasping for breath. Jia Zheng stepped forward, bowed, and said with an ingratiating smile, “In this oppressive heat, Mother, what has angered you so greatly that you have come in person? If you had something to say, you had only to summon your son and give him your instructions.” At this Grandmother Jia stopped, caught her breath for a moment, and said sternly, “So it is me you are addressing! I do indeed have instructions to give, but alas, in all my life I have failed to raise a good son. So whom am I to speak to?” Realizing that her words boded ill, Jia Zheng hurriedly knelt and said tearfully, “A son disciplines his own son only in the hope that he may bring honor to his ancestors. How can I, as your son, endure such words from you, Mother?” Grandmother Jia spat at him. “One word from me is more than you can bear, yet after laying into Baoyu so mercilessly with that board, do you imagine he could bear it? You say you discipline your son to honor your ancestors—but how did your own father discipline you?” As she spoke, tears began rolling down her cheeks. Still forcing a smile, Jia Zheng said, “You need not grieve, Mother. Your son merely lost his temper for a moment. From now on I shall never strike him again.” Grandmother Jia sneered, “There is no need to lose your temper with me or say such things out of spite. He is your son; it is no concern of mine whether you beat him or not. I daresay you have grown tired of us, mother and grandson alike. We had better leave you at once, so that everyone may be rid of everyone else!” She then ordered the sedan chairs and horses made ready. “Your wife, Baoyu, and I are returning to Nanjing at once!” The servants could only respond with hollow acknowledgments. Grandmother Jia then called to Lady Wang, “You need not weep anymore. Baoyu is young now, and you dote on him; but when he grows to manhood and becomes a high official, he may well forget that you are his mother. You would do better not to cherish him now; then perhaps you will be spared some vexation in years to come.” At this Jia Zheng hurriedly knocked his head on the floor and wept, “If Mother speaks so, there is no place left in the world for Jia Zheng to stand.” Grandmother Jia sneered, “It is clearly you who have left no place for me, yet now you complain of having no place yourself! Once we have gone, you will have peace of mind. Then let us see who will be here to permit you to beat him.” All the while she spoke, she kept ordering them to hurry and prepare the luggage, carriages, and sedan chairs for the journey home. Jia Zheng repeatedly kowtowed, imploring her forgiveness and confessing his fault.

p.src: Even as Grandmother Jia spoke, she remained anxious about Baoyu and hurried inside to see him. Finding that this beating was far worse than any before, she was both heartsick and furious, and embraced him, weeping without cease. Lady Wang, Xifeng, and the others consoled her for some time before she gradually stopped. Some maids and married servants came forward to help Baoyu to his feet, but Xifeng scolded them: “You witless creatures! Open your eyes and look! Beaten into such a state, how can he possibly walk even with your support? Hurry inside and bring out that rattan-seated daybed!” At her words they hurried inside and duly carried out the daybed. They lifted Baoyu onto it and, following Grandmother Jia, Lady Wang, and the others into the inner quarters, bore him to Grandmother Jia's rooms.

p.src: At that moment, seeing that Grandmother Jia’s anger had not yet fully subsided, Jia Zheng did not dare act as he pleased and followed her inside. When he looked at Baoyu, he saw that he had indeed beaten him severely. Then he looked at Lady Wang, who was crying out, now “my son,” now “my own flesh,” and lamenting, “If only you had died in Zhu’s place and Zhu had been spared, your father would not be driven to such anger, and all the care I have taken through half my life would not have been in vain. If anything should happen to you now and you leave me behind, whom am I to depend upon?” After pouring out these reproaches, she wept again for her “worthless son.” Hearing this, Jia Zheng’s spirit also failed him, and he regretted having dealt such merciless blows and reduced Baoyu to this state. He first tried to console Grandmother Jia, but she said through her tears, “Why are you still standing here instead of leaving? Have you still not satisfied your heart? Must you stay until you have watched him die before your very eyes?” Only after hearing this did Jia Zheng withdraw.

p.src: By then Aunt Xue, Baochai, Xiangling, Xiren, and Shi Xiangyun were all there as well. Xiren’s heart was full of grievance, though she could not openly show it. Seeing everyone crowded around Baoyu—some giving him water, others fanning him—and finding no way to lend a hand herself, she simply went out to the inner gate, had the pages fetch Beiming, and questioned him closely: “Everything was perfectly all right just now, so why did the beating start? And why did you not come sooner to warn us?” Beiming replied anxiously, “As ill luck would have it, I wasn’t there. I did not hear about it until the beating was already half over. I hurried to find out the cause, and it turned out to be about Qiguan and Sister Jinchuan.” “How did Master learn of it?” asked Xiren. Beiming said, “As for Qiguan, most likely Master Xue has long been jealous and, unable to vent his resentment, induced someone outside the household to stir up trouble and inflame Master against Baoyu. The matter of Jinchuan was reported by Third Master; at least, that is what I heard from Master’s attendants.” Both explanations fitted the circumstances, and Xiren believed them to be eight or nine parts true. When she returned, she found everyone tending Baoyu’s injuries. Once every necessary arrangement had been made, Grandmother Jia ordered them to “carry him carefully back to his room.” Everyone assented, and with many hands working at once, they hurriedly carried Baoyu into Happy Red Court and settled him on his own bed. After another long spell of confusion, the company gradually dispersed. Only then could Xiren come forward to attend him with care and ask exactly what had happened. What followed will be told in the next chapter.
